function.name: aero/force/lift-alpha
function.description: Lift with angle of attack and flap

function.name: aero/force/lift-slipstream
function.description: The propellers' slipstreams over the wing behind them. Each disc spans from 2 ft to 14 ft out from the centre line, so the slipstreams wash about 90 sq ft of wing each, flaps included, where the air moves at the aircraft's speed plus 1.5 times JSBSim's induced velocity (the slipstream half developed by the wing). The extra dynamic pressure lifts that wing at the wing's own lift coefficient. At take-off power it adds a sixth to the lift; with the engines throttled back the windmilling propellers take a little away; in cruise it is nothing. The Pilot's Notes (para. 43) stall "power on under typical approach conditions" at 90-95 knots, against 95-100 power off.

function.name: aero/force/drag-flaps
function.description: Flaps

function.name: aero/force/drag-gear
function.description: The undercarriage, down: "its high drag" (Pilot's Notes para. 57)

function.name: aero/force/drag-radiators
function.description: The radiator shutters, open. Set between HJ679's two climb rates, in MS gear at 10,400 ft and FS gear at 17,000 ft, both flown with them "fully open"; the level speeds were flown with them shut.

function.name: aero/force/drag-rudder
function.description: The fin's induced drag with the rudder over, as it is holding a failed engine: its side force squared over its span (about 8 ft) and the dynamic pressure

function.name: aero/force/drag-stopped-propellers
function.description: A stopped propeller - feathered, or seized - edge on to the air: JSBSim gives it none. About 0.4 sq ft of flat plate each.

function.name: aero/force/drag-sideslip
function.description: Sideslip

function.name: aero/force/drag-mach
function.description: Compressibility. The wing is thick, and the drag begins to rise gently from Mach 0.45 - set so that the trials' speeds at height and at sea level agree - and steeply towards the diving limits

function.name: aero/force/side-rudder
function.description: The fin's side force from the rudder: its yawing moment over the fin's arm, 23 ft of the 54.17 ft span

function.name: aero/moment/roll-sideslip
function.description: Dihedral effect

function.name: aero/moment/roll-aileron
function.description: "The controls are light and effective" (Pilot's Notes para. 42): about 50 degrees a second at 250 mph

function.name: aero/moment/roll-rudder
function.description: The same side force, 4 ft above the centre of gravity

function.name: aero/moment/pitch-stall
function.description: Past the stall the wing's flow separates from the root outward and the tailplane loses its downwash: the nose drops. "At the stall the aircraft pitches, the A.S.I. fluctuates and the nose drops gently" (Pilot's Notes para. 43).

function.name: aero/moment/pitch-elevator
function.description: The tailplane's volume, 0.51, with the elevator's effectiveness, in the tailplane's dynamic pressure

function.name: aero/moment/pitch-flaps
function.description: "Flaps down: nose up" (Pilot's Notes para. 42)

function.name: aero/moment/pitch-radiators
function.description: "Radiator shutters open: nose up" (Pilot's Notes para. 42)

function.name: aero/moment/pitch-gear
function.description: "Undercarriage down: nose down"

function.name: aero/moment/yaw-sideslip
function.description: Weathercock stability: "the directional and lateral stability is satisfactory"

function.name: aero/moment/yaw-slipstream
function.description: The propellers' slipstream on the fin. Both turn clockwise seen from behind, and their wakes turn with them: above the propellers' axes the air moves to starboard, so it strikes the fin from port and pushes the tail to starboard, the nose to port. JSBSim models the propellers' torque, gyroscopic moments and P-factor but not this, which on the ground with the tail down is what outweighs the torque's own tendency to turn the nose to starboard. In proportion to the thrust, and to each propeller's sense (JSBSim's: 1 clockwise from behind), set so that the take-off swing is to port and as slight as the Pilot's Notes say (para. 49, 1944).

function.name: aero/moment/yaw-rudder
function.description: The rudder's power: set so that, with one engine failed and its propeller windmilling, the speeds at which holding the aircraft straight takes full rudder fall as near as they can to both the Pilot's Notes' safety speeds, 170 knots at +18 boost and 155 at +9 - the model has them further apart, as the live engine's thrust at the two boosts puts them, and meets each within 6 knots
